summary: Iteration 13: Supabase Postgres migration validation for EasyBillsPay. Backend pytest: 16/17 PASS (1 critical fail: /api/auth/register 500). Frontend E2E (Playwright): customer login + dashboard + bills + bill intelligence (AI summary) + annual plan (forecast w/ Recharts chart + $5657.89 annual / $509.21 smoothed / Peak Jul 2026 / $91.04 variance + savings 93%->100% + category breakdown) + subscription (3 tiers, Basic Current Plan state) + payment plan (Weekly $120.37 / Fortnightly $240.75 / Monthly $521.62) all PASS. Admin login authenticates but does NOT auto-redirect to /admin; direct navigation to /admin renders Admin Panel correctly with role-gated sidebar. Most data flows from Supabase (6 seeded bills visible: AGL Energy, Origin Energy, Origin Gas, Sydney Water, Aussie Broadband; wallet $500). Migration successful EXCEPT registration.

critical.issue: Returns 500 — postgrest APIError PGRST204: 'Could not find the subscription_active column of users in the schema cache'. The User Pydantic model (server.py:153) has `subscription_active: bool = True` but the Supabase users table schema (schema.sql) is missing this column. Insert fails for every new registration.

minor.issue: Returns 404 — no health endpoint exists (was not present pre-migration either).
passlib bcrypt version warning: 'AttributeError: module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' — non-fatal, hashing still works.

integration_issues.issue: After successful admin login, app redirects to /dashboard (customer view) rather than /admin. User must manually navigate to /admin to see Admin Panel. Review request expected: 'Admin login redirects to admin dashboard'. Admin Panel itself works when accessed directly.

Stat cards on /admin (Financial Overview) appear as empty skeleton placeholders on initial load — could not confirm whether real numbers render (snapshot may be pre-data). /api/admin/financial-overview returns 200 so this is likely a render race, but worth verifying.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix /api/auth/register — either (a) add `subscription_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE` column to users table in schema.sql + re-run migration, or (b) drop `subscription_active` from User model / strip it from user_dict before sdb.insert_one. Recommend (a) for parity with original Mongo schema.
Add role-based redirect in frontend Login: if user.role==='admin' route to /admin instead of /dashboard.
Verify Admin Panel Financial Overview cards populate with data (may be a loading-state render bug).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:153 User model field `subscription_active` is not in Supabase users table — schema drift between Pydantic model and Postgres DDL. Run a schema-sync check at startup.
supabase_db.py insert_one passes full dict; any extra Pydantic-only field raises PGRST204. Either filter fields against a column allowlist or align schema strictly.
Auth payload uses key `token` (not `access_token`) — inconsistent with common conventions; ensure docs match.
/api/auth/register and other write paths should wrap APIError in 400/500 with a meaningful message instead of bubbling raw 500.
Bills response returns `provider` instead of `biller_name` — keep field naming consistent across collections/tables.
passlib bcrypt warning indicates bcrypt>=4 incompatibility; pin bcrypt<4 in requirements.txt or upgrade passlib.

CORE FUNCTIONALITY INTACT: login, bills CRUD, payment plan calc, payment-plan/current, bill intelligence (GPT ~10-15s), v2 predict-bills, v2 plan-health (returns {health:null,message:'No active plan.'} when no plan selected — accepted), v2 savings-comparison, v2 subscription/tiers (3 tiers Basic Free / Standard $9.90 / Premium $19.90), v2 subscription/current, notifications list (reserved 'read' column works), admin/users, admin/stats, admin/financial-overview, admin/customer-analytics. rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: User Pydantic model in server.py defines `subscription_active: bool = True`. During registration this flag is included in user_dict and passed to sdb.insert_one('users', user_dict). The Supabase migration of schema.sql did NOT create a `subscription_active` column on the users table, so PostgREST rejects the insert with code PGRST204.
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: POST /api/auth/register with {email,password,full_name} → 500 Internal Server Error. Backend log: postgrest.exceptions.APIError: {'message': \"Could not find the 'subscription_active' column of 'users' in the schema cache\", 'code': 'PGRST204'}
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN subscription_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE; (and add it to schema.sql so re-provisions stay consistent). Then NOTIFY pgrst 'reload schema' (or restart PostgREST) so the schema cache picks it up. Alternatively, remove the field from User model if unused.
